title: Ethiopian Beef Soup
localName: ሲሮ ወጥ / የሥጋ ሾርባ — Yesiga Shorba
community: All of Ethiopia — the restorative bone broth
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Yesiga Shorba — beef bones and meat simmered for 90 minutes with onion, garlic, ginger, and Ethiopian spices into a deep, restorative broth. The healing soup of Ethiopia — given to the sick, the recovering, and the new mother.
longDesc: Ethiopian beef soup is the simplest expression of the country's deeply nourishing cooking philosophy — good bones, water, time, and a few spices produce a soup of genuine healing power. Given to new mothers, to the sick, and drunk from a cup on cold mornings in the highlands.
steps: Place bones and meat in pot. Cover with cold water. Bring to a boil.
Skim foam thoroughly — 5 minutes of skimming.
Add onion, garlic, ginger, turmeric, pepper, and coriander.
Simmer on lowest heat for 80—90 minutes.
Remove meat from bones. Return meat to broth.
Season. Garnish with coriander. Serve with lime.
chefTips: Skim foam thoroughly — determines the clarity and cleanliness of the broth.
The lowest possible simmer produces the clearest broth.
commonMistakes: Boiling instead of simmering — cloudy result.
cookingScience: See TZA034 for bone broth cooking science.
sustainabilityTips: Uses bones that might otherwise be discarded — the most complete use of the animal.
servedWith: With injera for a light meal
culturalNote: Ethiopian beef soup is the nourishment of care — the food that Ethiopian families make when someone needs healing. The slow simmering of bones is an act of patience and love.
